title: Pepper-spray role in death to be probed
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit is looking into the death of a 41-year-old man who was pepper-sprayed by police early yesterday morning.
Robert Walker died while being rushed to hospital after an altercation with police outside a house on Woodbine Avenue near Queen Street, Rose Hong of the SIU said.

Triya Glassey, who lives on Woodbine Avenue, said she heard screaming outside her bedroom window and looked out to see a naked man surrounded by a number of police officers. She said he was standing in the middle of the street and was lunging at police.
She said he appeared "manic" and "crazed" and that she saw the officers spray Mr. Walker but they never appeared to touch him.
She said the spray had "almost zero effect" and that Mr. Walker lunged at police for up to five more minutes before collapsing.
He was taken by ambulance and "exhibited medical distress" during the trip to hospital, Ms. Hong said. He was pronounced dead on arrival at St. Michael's Hospital.
An autopsy was performed about noon yesterday. Investigators will receive the coroner's report.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates any injury, death or sex assault that occurs during police operations.
